articles.title: Caitlin Clark doesn't want to know anything about the WNBA finals or Angel Reese while she watches a different kind of basketball
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star turned her attention to the NBA as she attended the Pacers’ home opener
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star turned her attention to the NBA as she attended the Pacers’ home opener
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark was back courtside in Indianapolis on Friday night, but this time the Indiana Fever superstar was watching a different basketball team take center stage.

Clark attended the Indiana Pacers ’ home opener against the Dallas Mavericks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, showing her support for Tyrese Haliburton as he played his first home game since returning from a devastating Achilles injury.

Her appearance came while the WNBA Finals continued without the Fever , who were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs.

With the championship series between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries generating plenty of attention, Clark’s decision to spend the evening watching the NBA offered a reminder that her basketball interests extend beyond her own league.

There is no indication that Clark was deliberately avoiding news about the Finals or Angel Reese . However, her appearance at the Pacers game put her in the spotlight at a time when Reese is competing for a WNBA championship with Atlanta.

Clark and Haliburton have developed a close friendship through their shared connection to Indiana basketball.

The Fever guard has supported the Pacers star during his recovery, while Haliburton has also made appearances at Fever games, highlighting the relationship between the state's two professional basketball franchises.

The occasion was particularly meaningful for Haliburton , whose return to the court had been one of the major talking points surrounding the start of the NBA season.

Clark supports Haliburton as the Pacers begin a new chapter

Haliburton had been sidelined since tearing his right Achilles tendon during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The injury came at a devastating moment for Indiana, which had reached the deciding game of the championship series before losing its star guard.

He subsequently missed the entire 2025-26 campaign while recovering, leaving the Pacers without one of their most important players.

His competitive return arrived on Wednesday, when Indiana opened its season against the New Orleans Pelicans .

Haliburton delivered an impressive performance, scoring 23 points and recording 12 assists in a dramatic 123-120 victory. He also played a decisive role in the closing stages, helping the Pacers secure the win.

Friday's game therefore represented another milestone in his comeback, marking his first appearance at Gainbridge Fieldhouse since the injury that ended his previous season.

Clark's presence showed her support for a player who has experienced the emotional and physical challenges of a lengthy rehabilitation.

Haliburton had previously attended a Fever game against the Phoenix Mercury on June 22, 2026, when he even helped retrieve a basketball that had become stuck behind the backboard.

That moment illustrated how the two Indiana stars have embraced their roles as representatives of the state's basketball community.

For Clark, attending the Pacers game also provided an opportunity to enjoy the sport away from the pressures of her own season. The Fever had already completed their campaign, giving her time to follow the NBA as Haliburton resumed his career.

The evening did not, however, end with a victory for the home team. Dallas defeated Indiana 121-105, spoiling the Pacers' home opener despite the excitement surrounding Haliburton's return.

Angel Reese and the WNBA Finals continue without Clark

While Clark watched from Indianapolis, Reese was helping Atlanta pursue the first championship in franchise history.

The Dream entered the Finals against the Golden State Valkyries after sweeping the New York Liberty in the semifinals. Reese had been a major contributor to Atlanta's playoff run, establishing herself as one of the team's leading performers during a successful first season with the franchise.

The Finals have already produced several compelling performances. Golden State won the opening game 68-64, but Atlanta responded with a 79-65 victory in Game 2, with Reese recording 30 points and 16 rebounds.

The Dream then won Game 3 by a score of 97-71, taking a 2-1 series lead into Saturday's fourth matchup.

Reese's involvement in the championship series inevitably brings renewed attention to her long-running public rivalry with Clark , which dates back to their college basketball days.

Their matchups have become major talking points among fans, with discussions about their respective performances often extending well beyond the court.

Nevertheless, Clark's attendance at an NBA game should not automatically be interpreted as a statement about Reese or the Finals.

The Fever star was there to support Haliburton during an important moment in his comeback, and the two players have consistently demonstrated mutual support through their connection to Indiana basketball.

With Clark's offseason underway and the WNBA championship still to be decided, the two storylines are unfolding separately.

For one evening, the focus was on Haliburton's return and the Pacers' attempt to start their new campaign strongly, rather than on the Finals race in the WNBA.

articles.summary: The matching two-piece set and short skirt are more understated than some of Angel’s previous looks. But her heels, height and smooth, confident stride make the entrance impossible to miss.
articles.body: The matching two-piece set and short skirt are more understated than some of Angel’s previous looks. But her heels, height and smooth, confident stride make the entrance impossible to miss. Relaxed, happy and focused, she carries that unmistakable Angel presence with her. The look is soft; the presence is unmistakable. That “Angel” is always with her. And she’s walking into Game 4 after delivering 21 points and 12 rebounds to help Atlanta take a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals.

articles.title: Angel Reese’s simple striped look shows off her legs, but her Game 4 walk is pure star power
articles.standfirst: Reese arrives in a fitted, wine-and-rose striped two-piece and heels, carrying herself with a calm confidence
articles.summary: Reese arrives in a fitted, wine-and-rose striped two-piece and heels, carrying herself with a calm confidence
articles.body:
A ngel Reese’s outfit is more understated than some of the looks she has worn before: a matching two-piece set with thin vertical stripes in reddish and pink tones, a short skirt and heels. But as she walks through the arena hallway, the look becomes secondary to the way she carries herself. Her stride is smooth and unhurried; she seems happy, relaxed and focused.

There is no need for an extravagant entrance. Reese’s height, heels and easy cadence make her presence impossible to miss . She looks completely at home in the Finals spotlight and she arrives with Atlanta just two wins away from its first WNBA championship.

Angel Reese has made every Finals game count

Reese is coming off a 21-point, 12-rebound double-double in Atlanta’s 97-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3. She has recorded a double-double in all three games of the Finals: 14 points and 12 rebounds in the opener, 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, and another 21-and-12 performance on Wednesday. She is the youngest player to record double-doubles in three consecutive WNBA Finals games.

Her performances have helped Atlanta turn the series around. The Dream lost the opener, 68-64, but answered with a 79-65 win in Game 2 the first Finals victory in franchise history. They followed it with a 26-point blowout to take a 2-1 lead. The latest win was a team effort, with Rhyne Howard, Naz Hillmon, Isobel Borlase and Jordin Canada joining Reese in double figures.

Atlanta has also taken over the third quarter, outscoring Golden State 63-35 in that period across the first three games. In Game 3, the score was tied at 49 before the Dream pulled away. That surge, along with Reese’s work inside, has made it harder for the Valkyries to find their footing.

The Dream reached the Finals for the first time since 2013 after sweeping the Washington Mystics and New York Liberty. Now they have a chance to take a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series. A win would leave Atlanta one victory from the first title in franchise history; a Valkyries win would tie the series and shift the pressure back to the Dream.

Game 4 tips off Saturday at 1 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena, with coverage on NBC and Peacock. Reese’s walk into the arena is composed and carefree, but the opportunity in front of her is enormous: another win would bring Atlanta to the edge of the championship it has been chasing for years.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham becomes Angel Reese’s best ally in shifting the dynamic for Atlanta in the WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham weighs in on Angel Reese’s body language after her explosive Finals performance
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham weighs in on Angel Reese’s body language after her explosive Finals performance
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has shared a different perspective on Angel Reese’s emotional reaction during the WNBA Finals, suggesting the Atlanta Dream star’s frustration may have helped her team recognize what needed to change.

Reese attracted attention in Game 2 against the Golden State Valkyries after repeatedly calling for the ball in the post.

When teammates chose another option, she responded with animated gestures, sparking debate about her body language.

However, Cunningham believes the moment carried a message Atlanta needed to hear.

Speaking on her No Hesitation podcast, the Indiana Fever guard admitted Reese could have handled the situation better.

“Do I like the body language? Do I think that it could have been better? Absolutely,” said Cunningham . “And I think if she watches this back, I think she could have said the same thing.

“But three, sometimes you gotta do it. If your team’s not getting you the damn ball, then if you see one of your star players getting frustrated and getting pissed off, then it’s like, ‘Oh, they’re not messing around.

“We need to get her the damn ball.’ I think the coaching staff saw it; I think everyone on the bench saw it; her teammates felt the energy; and she did what she needed to do in order to put yet another game on her back.”

In Game 2, Reese had been working to establish position near the basket, but the ball went elsewhere. Her frustration quickly became a talking point, but talk quickly shifted back to her performance.

Reese finished with 30 points and 16 rebounds, shooting 10-for-16 from the field as Atlanta won 79-65 to tie the series. Her presence in the paint gave the Dream a boost and showed how influential she could be when involved consistently.

Reese’s response has changed Atlanta’s championship push

Reese carried that momentum into Game 3, helping Atlanta defeat Golden State 97-71. She recorded 21 points and 12 rebounds, giving the Dream a 2-1 series advantage and putting them within two wins of the championship.

The performance extended her run of consecutive Finals double-doubles, underscoring her impact on the biggest stage.

Head coach Karl Smesko has praised Reese’s development, highlighting her determination to improve throughout the season.

“She very well might be the most improved player from the beginning of the season to right now,” Smesko said.

Cunningham’s defense of Reese highlights the difference between showing frustration and allowing it to damage team chemistry. While expressive body language can invite criticism, it can also signal that a team needs to adjust.

With Game 4 approaching in Atlanta, the Dream have a chance to strengthen their hold on the series. Golden State will be eager to respond, while Reese’s teammates will need to keep finding her in advantageous positions.

Reese’s reaction may remain a subject of debate, but her production has made its own statement.

Reese attracted attention in Game 2 against the Golden State Valkyries after repeatedly calling for the ball in the post.
When teammates chose another option, she responded with animated gestures, sparking debate about her body language.
However, Cunningham believes the moment carried a message Atlanta needed to hear.
Speaking on her No Hesitation podcast, the Indiana Fever guard admitted Reese could have handled the situation better.
“Do I like the body language? Do I think that it could have been better? Absolutely,” said Cunningham . “And I think if she watches this back, I think she could have said the same thing.

articles.title: Frustration for Angel Reese: the Valkyries storm Atlanta and level the Finals again
articles.standfirst: Another great game by Gabby Williams with 17 points
articles.summary: Another great game by Gabby Williams with 17 points
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream (62-67) in the fourth game of the WNBA Finals played this Saturday, thanks to their stars Gabby Williams and Ceci Zandalasini returning to their best form ( 17 and 10 points respectively ) and tying the series for the championship ring (2-2).

The California team responded to the pressure after suffering two heavy defeats in a row, in a game in which they gave the home side no chance at any point, as they lost their first home game in the "playoffs" this season.

The Valkyries' strong defense on Angel Reese did not allow her to shine as she had in previous games, and she ended up with a poor 2/12 from the field.

After suffering their worst defeat of the season in Game 3 of the Finals (-26 points) , coach Natalie Nakase made two changes to Golden State's starting lineup, bringing in Tiff Hayes and Kaila Charles in search of greater offensive efficiency, leaving Italian player Zandalasini on the bench.

However, the plan did not work because the start followed the pattern of the last few matchups: no accuracy for the Californians and the Dream came out firing.

After a timeout by Nakase midway through the first half, and above all with the introduction of Cecilia Zandalasini onto the court, the Valkyries' energy changed on defense (with four consecutive steals and holding star Reese to 0 points in the first quarter) and, on offense, with a 12-0 run.

The intensity increased in the second period, and Golden State's two biggest stars showed up when their team needed them most.

"Ceci," with a nice drive through the middle, added a 2+1, which, together with the contribution of forward Gabby Williams (with seven almost consecutive points), gave the visitors their biggest lead on the scoreboard up to that point (+16).

Atlanta got a taste of its own medicine. It is the team that steals the most balls per game in the American league, but in the first half its 14 turnovers. doomed it.

In the restart, the Dream looked more like the energetic team that had come in on a two-game winning streak to rally in the series. A wing three-pointer by Australian Borlase cut the deficit to just 6 points (40-46).

But the "Violets" showed character and responded every time Atlanta got closer on the scoreboard to keep their distance.

In the final minutes, with the home side pouring forward urged on by their crowd, Tiff Hayes put the team on her back with productive drives to the basket, and a long-range three-pointer by Burton gave Golden State some breathing room (55-64 with 4:19 remaining).

The excitement lasted until the end. Rhyne Howard answered with an and-one to Veronica Burton's fade-away with 28 seconds remaining and Atlanta trailing by four , but two consecutive missed three-pointers by the home team sealed the victory for the Valkyries .

Next Monday they will return to San Francisco for the fifth game, which will be played at the Valhalla arena to break the tie in a finals series that will be decided in a best-of-seven format.

Referees: Roy Gulbeyan, Tim Greene and Marcy Williams.

Notes: game corresponding to the fourth match of the WNBA Finals at the State Farm Arena in Atlanta (United States).

articles.title: A warning regarding what could happen with the Indiana Fever: "Keep Caitlin Clark happy or she's gone"
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark’s future in Indiana comes under scrutiny after Fever part ways with two top executives
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s future in Indiana comes under scrutiny after Fever part ways with two top executives
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever’s recent front-office shake-up has raised fresh questions about Caitlin Clark’s future, with former college basketball player and WNBA analyst Rachel DeMita warning that the franchise must give its superstar compelling reasons to stay.

Clark recently reaffirmed her commitment to Indiana, stating, “No matter what, I’m going to be here.” However, DeMita believes that loyalty shouldn’t prevent the star guard from exploring other opportunities if the organization fails to help her reach her full potential.

“Here’s the truth of the matter, it’s really something like keep Caitlin happy or she’s gone,” DeMita said on her Courtside Club podcast.

“I’m going to use Angel Reese as the example because I’ve said it many times. I think Angel leaving Chicago was the best thing that she could have done for her career. Caitlin can also do that, and Caitlin Clark should do that if she likes.”

Her warning comes as Indiana faces significant organizational changes following a disappointing postseason campaign.

Fever face crucial decisions after front-office shake-up

On Friday, October 23, team president Kelly Krauskopf announced her departure from the organization. Hours later, the Fever confirmed that general manager and chief operating officer Amber Cox had also been dismissed, leaving two senior leadership positions in transition.

The developments have intensified scrutiny of Indiana’s direction after the team finished sixth in the standings and suffered a first-round playoff elimination against the Las Vegas Aces.

The back-to-back departures have also fueled speculation about whether further changes could follow.

However, reports from USA TODAY’s Meghan L. Hall indicate that head coach Stephanie White is expected to retain her position for the 2027 season.

White has faced considerable attention during her second stint with Indiana, particularly because of the expectations surrounding Clark and the franchise.

Although the Fever made the playoffs in consecutive seasons under her leadership, their latest early exit has raised questions about what must change for the team to become a genuine championship contender.

Clark , meanwhile, delivered an impressive 2026 campaign, averaging a career-high 22.3 points, 8.3 assists, four rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. Despite those numbers, Indiana's postseason disappointment highlighted the work still required to turn individual performances into sustained playoff success.

DeMita believes the Fever must recognize how valuable Clark is to their future. Improving the supporting roster, establishing a clearer offensive system and strengthening the front office could all help create an environment in which the young superstar can thrive.

Reese’s experience offers a useful comparison. After two seasons with Chicago, she moved to Atlanta, illustrating how changing teams can provide fresh opportunities. Nevertheless, Clark hasn’t announced any intention to leave Indiana.

The leadership vacancies give the Fever an opportunity to reassess their basketball operations and build a stronger foundation around their core players. Finding executives capable of attracting talent and assembling a championship-caliber roster will be particularly important.

Clark has publicly expressed her commitment, and White is expected to remain head coach. Whether that stability continues will depend on how effectively Indiana addresses its shortcomings.

articles.title: Angel Reese admits her mistake in WNBA Finals Game 4: a performance to forget
articles.standfirst: Reese finished with eight points and nine rebounds, a far cry from the dominance she showed in the previous two games
articles.summary: Reese finished with eight points and nine rebounds, a far cry from the dominance she showed in the previous two games
articles.body:
A ngel Reese took responsibility and explained why she couldn’t find her rhythm when Atlanta needed her most. After dominating Games 2 and 3, the Dream star had an unusually difficult night against Golden State, scoring just eight points and grabbing nine rebounds in a 67-62 loss that tied the WNBA Finals at 2-2.

After the game, Reese acknowledged what went wrong around the basket. “I think I rushed a lot of my shots and I didn’t take my time and finish around the basket like I’ve been doing in the last three games. It happens,” she said at the press conference, looking visibly frustrated.

Golden State contained Angel Reese and tied the series

The Valkyries’ defense made every possession tougher. Golden State changed its starting lineup and stuck to its game plan, sending more defenders to cut Reese off. She finished 2-for-12 from the field, didn’t score in the first quarter and had five turnovers and three fouls by halftime.

Atlanta’s mistakes also helped create the gap. The Valkyries controlled the turnover battle in the first half, forcing 16 while committing just four and taking a 16-point lead into the break. The Dream fought back after halftime, but couldn’t complete the comeback.

Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 19 points, while Isobel Borlase and Jordin Canada added 10 apiece. For Golden State, Gabby Williams finished with 17 points; Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton scored 13 each, and Kiah Stokes grabbed 16 rebounds.

The 67-62 win evened the WNBA Finals at 2-2, keeping Atlanta from moving within one victory of the championship. Game 5 is set for Monday, Oct. 26, in San Francisco at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Angel Reese’s big defensive moment isn’t enough as WNBA Finals shift again
articles.standfirst: The All-Star celebrated the block before turning toward her teammates, visibly energized by the stop
articles.summary: The All-Star celebrated the block before turning toward her teammates, visibly energized by the stop
articles.body:
A ngel Reese’s defensive intensity gave the Atlanta Dream a spark in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals , but it was not enough to prevent a 67-62 loss to the Golden State Valkyries, leaving the championship series tied 2-2. Reese finished with eight points, nine rebounds, three assists, one steal and three blocks. Her rejection of French star Gabby Williams in the first quarter became one of the game’s defining moments, showcasing the defensive presence and emotion that have helped fuel Atlanta’s Finals run.

The play also prompted a pointed observation from the NBC Sports broadcast. "You see the passion, you see the energy. That’s the difference in mentality for Atlanta,” the commentator said.

But by the final buzzer, Golden State had answered Atlanta’s recent surge with a crucial victory, ensuring the series would head into its next game level rather than leaving the Valkyries one loss away from elimination.

Reese’s defense makes an impression

With 2:28 remaining in the first quarter and Golden State leading 11-7, Williams brought the ball toward the basket with Reese tracking her closely. As Williams attempted to evade the Dream forward and finish at the rim, Reese swatted the shot away before it could reach the basket.

Reese celebrated the block before turning toward her teammates, visibly energized by the defensive stop.

The sequence reflected the approach she has brought to the series since Atlanta’s Game 1 defeat. After going scoreless in the second half of the opener, Reese said she needed to be more aggressive. The Dream subsequently responded with two victories to take a 2-1 lead.

In Game 4, Reese again made her presence felt defensively, recording three blocks and pulling down nine rebounds. Her eight points, however, came in a game where Atlanta struggled to generate enough offense to secure the win.

The defeat also complicated the Finals MVP conversation. Reese’s all-around contributions have made her one of the central figures in Atlanta’s run, but Golden State’s response means the series remains wide open.

Valkyries respond when the pressure rises

Golden State entered the Finals with one of the league’s strongest defensive identities, having posted a 99.3 defensive rating during the regular season. Gabby Williams earned All-Defensive First Team honors, while Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton were named to the Second Team.

That reputation came under pressure when Atlanta scored 97 points in Game 3, setting a Dream franchise record for points in a Finals game. The Valkyries, who had swept the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals, now have a chance to build on their Game 4 performance.

Their 67-62 win demonstrated that they could slow Atlanta down after the Dream had found their rhythm offensively. The low-scoring result also underscored how dramatically the matchup shifted from Game 3. This time, Atlanta could not translate its energy into enough points to maintain control of the series.

The 67-62 result changes the pressure on both teams. Atlanta missed its opportunity to take a 3-1 lead, while Golden State avoided falling into a difficult position heading into the next game. The challenge for Angel Reese is to maintain her defensive impact while helping the Dream find more scoring against a Valkyries team that rediscovered its defensive edge.

articles.title: Angel Reese's Game 4 performance came with a silver lining despite brutal loss
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream couldn't get anything going offensively against the Golden State Valkyries, and the WNBA Finals are now tied at 2-2.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream couldn't get anything going offensively against the Golden State Valkyries, and the WNBA Finals are now tied at 2-2.
articles.body:
The arrow was pointing way up for the Atlanta Dream heading into Saturday. With a 2-1 series lead and playing at home, the Dream could have come within one win of a championship with a victory at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia on Saturday.

The shots simply weren't falling for Atlanta, though. A 33% team field goal percentage , paired with nine missed free throws , kept the Dream from getting a crucial win. The Golden State Valkyries won 67-62 and have now tied the series at 2-2 with home court advantage in their favor.

There were many culprits for Atlanta's offensive struggles, but Angel Reese has taken the brunt of the blame. Reese shot a measly 2-of-12 from the field, while also committing six turnovers . Despite many fans online lighting into Reese for her performance, there was at least a silver lining for her: She actually led the team in plus-minus .

Angel Reese and Alisha Gray led the team with a +1 plus-minus in Dream's Game 4 loss to Valkyries

Reese was a +1 for the game, as was Alisha Gray . They led the Dream, while the other three starters were all negative: Jordin Canada with -1 , Naz Hilllmon with -4 , and Rhyne Howard with -6 . The bench was particularly detrimental, as DeWanna Bonner was -9 and Isobel Borlase was -7 . No one else played more than a minute.

Even though she struggled to score and keep possession throughout the game, Reese still contributed in other ways like she always does . She grabbed nine rebounds , handed out three assists , blocked three shots , and added one steal . That was enough to make her impact an overall positive one in Game 4.

The Dream only lost by five points despite a lot of things going wrong on Saturday. But if they continue to struggle to score, they might not be able to get back into the series before it's too late.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark fans urge her to follow Angel Reese’s path to the WNBA Finals as coach Stephanie White may stay
articles.standfirst: Indiana’s front-office shake-up brought major changes
articles.summary: Indiana’s front-office shake-up brought major changes
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark is entering her third WNBA season as one of the league’s biggest stars and most recognizable faces. But while Angel Reese is playing in the WNBA Finals with the Atlanta Dream , Clark still hasn’t reached the championship series with the Indiana Fever. That contrast has some fans asking whether she should follow Reese’s lead and find a new home.

The conversation grew louder as Indiana began reshaping its front office. Some Fever fans had hoped the changes would include head coach Stephanie White , whom they believe has not found the right way to get the most out of Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell together.

Indiana has confirmed that president of basketball and business operations Kelly Krauskopf is stepping down and that general manager and COO Amber Cox has left the organization. The team plans to conduct a national search for its next GM, but has not announced a replacement.

Caitlin Clark had nothing but gratitude for Stephanie White

White, meanwhile, is expected to remain Indiana’s head coach , according to ESPN sources, though the Fever has not officially confirmed the report. Her coaching has drawn criticism from fans who feel Clark is sometimes underused or pushed into the background.

But Clark herself spoke warmly about White after the season, saying, “I really appreciate Steph.” She also praised the time and effort the coaching staff put into helping the team succeed and said she was grateful for them.

That response doesn’t mean Clark publicly campaigned for White to return. It does show that the relationship may look different from the outside than it does inside the team.

Clark also acknowledged that when a season falls short of expectations, responsibility belongs to the players as well as the coaching staff. Reese’s move to Atlanta wasn’t a guaranteed ticket to the Finals. She arrived in a trade without knowing how the season would unfold, and the Dream hadn’t reached the championship series since 2013, a 13-year wait.

Now, after Atlanta’s 67-62 loss in Game 4, the series is tied 2-2, and Reese has admitted she rushed her shots and didn’t give herself enough time to finish around the basket. Her path is remarkable, but it’s no promise that changing teams will lead to a title.

Still, it’s easy to understand why Fever fans are bringing up Clark’s future now. Indiana is making changes in its front office, while White is reportedly expected to stay as head coach.

articles.title: The harshest criticism of Angel Reese: “Just embarrassed herself on the biggest stage”
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese suffered a tough blow this Saturday, October 24.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese suffered a tough blow this Saturday, October 24.
articles.body:
After two standout performances that had kept the team in contention for the WNBA title, Game 4 of the Finals ended very differently for Atlanta’s star, who struggled to find her rhythm on the court.

The Golden State Valkyries secured a 67-62 victory , tied the series, and put Reese at the center of criticism over her offensive struggles.

Angel Reese had a difficult afternoon

Reese finished the game with just eight points and nine rebounds after making only two of her 12 field-goal attempts, shooting 16.7% . Her struggles to find the basket made a significant difference in a game where every score could have brought Atlanta closer to victory.

Foul trouble and turnovers added to her difficulties, further complicating her performance. Although the loss reflected the Dream’s overall performance, Reese’s individual numbers drew particular attention given the contrast with her previous outings.

Atlanta had an opportunity to take the series lead and move closer to the championship, but ultimately fell to a Valkyries team that took advantage of the result to even things up.

Yahoo delivers harsh criticism of Angel Reese

The Atlanta star’s performance did not go unnoticed by journalist Landon Kardian , who published an article on Yahoo with a blunt headline: “Angel Reese Just Embarrassed Herself on the Biggest Stage,” a phrase that sharply questions her performance in the game.

The criticism focused on her offensive struggles and inability to consistently convert the opportunities she had near the basket.

The WNBA Finals will be decided in Game 5

Following this difficult performance, the championship could be decided on Monday, October 26 , when the two teams meet at Chase Center in San Francisco.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark reclaims her place in the WNBA while Angel Reese takes a step back in the WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: Clark returns to the WNBA’s elite ranks, while Reese and the Atlanta Dream face renewed pressure after their Finals setback
articles.summary: Clark returns to the WNBA’s elite ranks, while Reese and the Atlanta Dream face renewed pressure after their Finals setback
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has returned to WNBA’s elite company, earning a place on the 2026 All-WNBA First Team, while Angel Reese faces the challenge of rediscovering her scoring touch as the championship series intensifies.

Clark’s selection recognizes another impressive season with the Indiana Fever, where her scoring ability and playmaking have established her among the league’s most influential guards.

She averaged 22.5 points and 8.4 assists per game, ranking third in scoring and tying for the league lead in assists.

The honor marks Clark’s second first-team selection after earning the distinction as a rookie in 2024. She joins teammate Kelsey Mitchell , who averaged 24.7 points per game, on a Fever backcourt that delivered exceptional offensive production throughout the regular season.

Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson , New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart and Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles complete the first team. Wilson followed another MVP-winning campaign with her sixth first-team selection, while Miles enjoyed an outstanding rookie season that earned her recognition among the league’s best players.

Despite their individual achievements, none of the first-team selections feature in the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries.

Angel Reese faces a response test as Finals pressure builds

While Clark celebrates her individual recognition, Reese is preparing for a crucial response after Atlanta’s momentum was interrupted in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals.

The Dream suffered a 67-62 defeat against the Valkyries on Saturday missing an opportunity to move within one victory of the championship. The result levelled the best-of-seven series at 2-2, increasing the pressure on both teams heading into the decisive stretch.

Reese , who was named the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year and earned a place on the All-WNBA Second Team, finished with eight points, nine rebounds, three assists, one steal and three blocks.

Her offensive struggles were particularly noticeable after two outstanding performances in the previous games. Reese recorded 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 before producing 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3. Against Golden State, however, she struggled to find her rhythm around the basket.

“I think I rushed a lot of my shots and I didn’t take my time and finish around the basket like I’ve been doing in the last 3 games,” Reese said after the defeat. She acknowledged the problem and emphasized her determination to improve in the next game.

Atlanta still has an opportunity to regain control of the series. Rhyne Howard led the Dream with 19 points and eight rebounds, while Jordin Canada and Isobel Borlase contributed 10 points apiece. Howard also earned second-team All-WNBA honors alongside Reese .

The Valkyries will now look to maintain their defensive intensity in Game 5 on Monday, October 26, at Chase Center.

articles.title: The two teams that could separate Sophie Cunningham from Caitlin Clark and give her the contract she wants
articles.standfirst: The 30-year-old guard will become an unrestricted free agent after completing a one-season contract with Indiana. Two teams are among the possible destinations, although for now there is no official confirmation of negotiations, and Cunningham has already made it clear that she is seeking stability and a multi-year deal.
articles.summary: The 30-year-old guard will become an unrestricted free agent after completing a one-season contract with Indiana. Two teams are among the possible destinations, although for now there is no official confirmation of negotiations, and Cunningham has already made it clear that she is seeking stability and a multi-year deal.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham will be one of the names to watch in the upcoming WNBA free agency. Portland Fire and Los Angeles Sparks have been mentioned as possible teams interested in the veteran shooting guard, although for now there is no official confirmation of contacts or negotiations. Indiana Fever, meanwhile, continues to appear as the main option to retain her, with the length of the next contract being one of the decisive factors.

Cunningham finished the 2026 season averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game in 43 appearances. She also made 41.9% of her three-pointers and was Indiana’s leading scorer off the bench, numbers that maintain her value within a team built around Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell.

A multi-year contract, the key condition

The length of the agreement is no minor detail for Cunningham. In April, she signed for one season with the Fever, on a reported $665,000 contract , and later clarified that her dissatisfaction was not related to the salary. “I just wanted more years because I love being here”, she explained at the time, noting that she was looking to establish herself permanently in Indiana.

The player also confirmed that she had received multi-year offers from other teams before deciding to remain with the Fever in 2026. At that time, Cunningham prioritized staying with a group where she felt comfortable, even though other destinations offered the contractual security she was looking for.

Indiana expressed interest in keeping her after the playoff elimination. Amber Cox, then the franchise's general manager, highlighted her leadership, experience, and ability to connect the locker room, in addition to her two seasons of strong perimeter play. However, Cox left her position on October 23, and the Fever began a nationwide search to find her replacement, a change that adds another variable to the team's decisions for 2027.

Portland and Los Angeles now appear among the possible alternatives for Cunningham, but it is still a market scenario . So far, there is no announced agreement or public confirmation that either of the two teams has initiated formal talks with the player.

Cunningham arrived in Indiana from Phoenix before the 2025 season and remained with the Fever for two campaigns. After recovering from the medial collateral ligament injury that prematurely ended her 2025 season, she returned in 2026 and once again established herself as one of the second unit’s main perimeter threats.

For now, there is no new contract announced .

Cunningham will be able to assess the market as an unrestricted free agent and, if Indiana intends to keep her alongside Clark and the rest of its core, the length of the offer appears to be one of the central points of the negotiation.

Portland Fire and Los Angeles Sparks appear as possibilities, but their interest will have to be confirmed when free agency begins to formally move.

articles.title: Crisis Solved: WNBA reaches agreement with Hawks over Game 6 arena clash
articles.standfirst: The Dream will retain their home-court advantage at State Farm Arena after negotiations produce a rare NBA and WNBA doubleheader
articles.summary: The Dream will retain their home-court advantage at State Farm Arena after negotiations produce a rare NBA and WNBA doubleheader
articles.body:
A championship game deserves a championship atmosphere, and the WNBA has secured precisely that for Game 6 of the Finals. Whether supporters can actually attend at the newly announced time, however, is another matter.

The league confirmed Monday that the Atlanta Dream will host the Golden State Valkyries at State Farm Arena on October 29, avoiding the possibility of moving one of the season's biggest games to a considerably smaller venue.

The agreement required cooperation from the Atlanta Hawks , who share the arena and were already scheduled to face the Cleveland Cavaliers that evening.

Instead of relocating either game, the organizations agreed to an unusual doubleheader. The WNBA Finals will begin at 12:30 p.m. ET, followed by the Hawks ' NBA matchup at 8 p.m.

While the compromise resolves the venue dispute, it leaves fans facing an inconvenient weekday tip-off.

The alternative would have been particularly disappointing for Atlanta, which has enjoyed tremendous support throughout its postseason run.

State Farm Arena accommodates approximately 17,000 spectators, compared with just 3,500 at Gateway Center Arena , the Dream's usual home venue.

Games 3 and 4 of the Finals attracted sellout crowds at State Farm Arena, demonstrating the demand for women's basketball in Atlanta.

WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert welcomed the agreement, emphasizing the importance of keeping the championship series at the larger venue.

"The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line," Engelbert said.

However, supporters hoping to attend must now reorganize their schedules, with the new start time creating obvious difficulties for people working or attending school.

Scheduling conflict forces unusual compromise

The Hawks ' existing commitments made finding an alternative date particularly difficult.

Atlanta faces the Miami Heat on Wednesday evening, leaving insufficient recovery time for the team to accommodate an early Thursday NBA game.

Moving the Hawks ' meeting with Cleveland to Friday would also complicate the Cavaliers ' schedule before their Saturday matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks .

Meanwhile, postponing Game 6 would have threatened the timing of a potential Game 7 in San Francisco, where the Golden State Warriors have upcoming home commitments.

The agreement avoids those complications and preserves the WNBA's existing championship schedule.

Atlanta Dream prepare for crucial Finals showdown

The series remains tied at 2-2 heading into Monday's Game 5 in California, meaning Thursday's contest could determine the championship.

Dream guard Jordin Canada welcomed the opportunity to return to State Farm Arena despite the unusual timing.

"The crowd has showed up and showed out for Games 3 and 4 so looking forward to being at State Farm for Game 6," Canada told reporters.

Thursday's game will be televised on USA Network and streamed through Peacock, with the league planning additional promotional efforts to raise awareness of the change.

A potential Game 7 remains scheduled for Saturday, October 31, at Chase Center in San Francisco.

The WNBA has protected the atmosphere surrounding its championship series, but the midday tip-off remains an awkward price for securing Atlanta's preferred venue.

articles.title: Angel Reese accused of playing dirty during Game 5 of the WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: The Golden State Valkyries are one win away from history after Kiah Stokes delivered a Finals masterpiece and pushed Atlanta Dream to the brink of elimination.
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries are one win away from history after Kiah Stokes delivered a Finals masterpiece and pushed Atlanta Dream to the brink of elimination.
articles.body:
A ngel Reese is, without a doubt, the player attracting the most attention in the WNBA Finals . But this time she has become the center of attention for fans because of her physical play, which many believe has crossed the line.

The Atlanta Dream forward is being accused of using her elbows in a violent manner against Golden State Valkyries players, particularly for the actions observed during the first quarter of Game 5 of the series.

Tough defeat for the Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese

Kiah Stokes delivered a huge performance with 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocks as the Golden State Valkyries moved one win away from their first WNBA championship, defeating the Atlanta Dream 64-55 in Game 5 of the Finals on Monday night.

The second-year expansion franchise now leads the series 3-2 and can clinch the title with a victory in Game 6 on Thursday in Atlanta .

While Angel Reese posted another strong rebounding night with 15 boards, five assists and seven points, she couldn’t replicate the dominant performances that helped Atlanta win the first two games of the series at Chase Center.

Stokes became the unlikely hero for Golden State on a night when leading scorer Gabby Williams struggled offensively. Williams finished with just nine points on 3-of-14 shooting, but the Valkyries once again showed the depth behind coach Natalie Nakase’s “strength in numbers” philosophy .

Veronica Burton matched Stokes with 13 points and eight rebounds, while veteran Tiffany Hayes added 12 points after earning another start following a lineup change that helped Golden State win Game 4.

The Valkyries entered halftime with a slim 25-22 lead, marking the lowest-scoring first half in WNBA Finals history. Neither team found rhythm from beyond the arc, combining to shoot just 5-of-29 from three-point range.

But Golden State took control in the second half, making the biggest plays when it mattered most. Stokes hit two crucial three-pointers, including one late in the third quarter and another with 7:21 remaining, sending the Chase Center crowd into a frenzy with chants of “Ki-ah! Ki-ah!”

The center also made history by recording three or more blocks in six consecutive playoff games, tying Lisa Leslie’s 2003 WNBA postseason record for the longest streak of its kind.

Atlanta struggled to keep pace, committing 17 turnovers that turned into 21 Golden State points. Despite a late push led by Rhyne Howard , the Dream couldn’t overcome the Valkyries’ defensive intensity and clutch execution.

Now, Atlanta faces elimination on Thursday in Game 6 at State Farm Arena, where the Dream must win to force a decisive Game 7 back at Chase Center on Saturday.

Golden State’s rapid rise has already exceeded expectations. When owner Joe Lacob secured the expansion franchise, he predicted a championship within five years. The Valkyries now stand just one victory away from making that bold promise a reality in only their second season.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham responds with love despite fierce backlash from fans over her flag-waving role at COTA
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player chose a simple social media gesture after some racing fans questioned her prominent role at Circuit of the Americas
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player chose a simple social media gesture after some racing fans questioned her prominent role at Circuit of the Americas
articles.body:
An invitation to participate in one of Formula 1 's biggest American races turned into an unexpected social media controversy for Sophie Cunningham , whose appearance at the United States Grand Prix divided fans over the growing influence of celebrity culture in motorsport.

The Indiana Fever guard attended Sunday's race at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas, where she was given the ceremonial responsibility of waving the checkered flag as Kimi Antonelli secured victory for Mercedes .

For Cunningham , it was an opportunity to experience Formula 1 from an unusual vantage point. However, her prominent role prompted questions among some supporters about why a basketball player had been chosen to mark the conclusion of the race.

The criticism quickly spread across social media, although Cunningham showed little interest in engaging with the controversy.

Instead, she left two heart emojis beneath an Instagram post celebrating her appearance, offering a positive reaction without directly addressing those who had questioned her involvement.

Cunningham 's selection became a talking point among fans who believe Formula 1 is placing increasing emphasis on celebrity appearances during Grand Prix weekends.

Some questioned whether the checkered flag ceremony should have been reserved for someone with a stronger connection to motorsport.

"Who the heck invited Sophie Cunningham to this?" one supporter wrote on X, reflecting the frustration expressed by a section of the audience.

The two-heart comment wasn't an explicit response to her critics, but it demonstrated that Cunningham remained positive about the experience despite the negative attention.

The basketball player embraced the event's Texas setting, wearing a cowboy hat and posting a photograph accompanied by the caption "YEE MF HAW."

Her participation came during a race weekend that attracted considerable attention beyond the traditional motorsport audience, with celebrities and athletes appearing throughout the paddock.

The United States Grand Prix has become one of Formula 1's most prominent American events, combining championship competition with entertainment and appearances from personalities across different industries.

That crossover appeal helps explain Cunningham 's invitation, even if not every supporter welcomed the decision.

The moment should have been a straightforward celebration of the winner, but the reaction demonstrated how even ceremonial appearances can generate controversy among Formula 1's expanding audience.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham has her sights set on Victoria"s Secret after seeing Angel Reese
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player revealed one of her biggest goals off the court.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player revealed one of her biggest goals off the court.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has had no problem showing her more personal side outside of basketball, and now the Indiana Fever player revealed one of the goals she would like to achieve in the future: to walk in the Victoria"s Secret fashion show someday.

Cunningham spoke about the subject during an episode of her podcast "No Hesitation" alongside Drew Hanlen, while they commented on the 2026 Victoria"s Secret Fashion Show. The WNBA player admitted that she is a big fan of the event and made it clear how excited she is about the possibility of being part of it someday.

Angel Reese has already paved the way for WNBA stars

“I think that’s my goal, to be a Victoria"s Secret angel someday,” Cunningham said during the conversation. She even joked about the possibility of sharing that experience with Christine, Hanlen’s wife: “It would be so much fun”.

The idea of seeing a WNBA star on that runway no longer seems strange. Angel Reese made history in 2025 by becoming the first professional athlete to walk in the Victoria"s Secret Fashion Show, opening an unprecedented door for league players.

Reese later strengthened her connection with the brand by also taking part in an additional campaign, consolidating a presence that transcended the courts and brought her image into the world of fashion.

Cunningham also spoke about some of the models she admires most. Among them, she especially mentioned Candice Swanepoel, as well as figures such as Gigi and Bella Hadid, Adriana Lima, and Alessandra Ambrosio.

The world of modeling is not entirely unfamiliar to Cunningham either. The player made her debut in Sports Illustrated Swimsuit in 2026, an experience that she herself had previously pointed out as one of the personal goals she wanted to achieve.

The 30-year-old American has significantly increased her exposure since arriving at Indiana Fever , combining her WNBA career with her podcast, commercial deals, and fashion-related appearances.

Participating in an event for Victoria"s Secret remains only an aspiration for Cunningham, and there is no announced agreement between the player and the brand. Meanwhile, her sporting future will also be one of the topics to follow during the WNBA offseason.

articles.title: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are backed into a corner after a tough Game 5 loss in the Finals
articles.standfirst: The Dream had a chance to turn the series around, but a forgettable offensive performance left them on the brink of elimination.
articles.summary: The Dream had a chance to turn the series around, but a forgettable offensive performance left them on the brink of elimination.
articles.body:
Their own worst enemy. Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream had a major opportunity in Game 5 of the WNBA Finals: put their previous loss behind them and take the lead in the championship race. But things did not go as planned, leaving them in a difficult position at a time when they could least afford it.

On Monday, October 26, the Dream faced the Golden State Valkyries at Chase Center in San Francisco , where fans packed the stands.

Angel Reese couldn't find her shot when it mattered most

Atlanta's star finished with just 7 points, making only 2 of her 8 field-goal attempts , a far cry from the offensive level she had displayed during some of her best performances in these Finals.

Foul trouble also complicated her night, limiting her playing time for much of the second quarter as Golden State's defense made it difficult for her to find room to attack. Even so, Reese contributed in other areas of the game, recording 15 rebounds and 5 assists .

After the game, Dream head coach Karl Smesko criticized the officiating, arguing that officials had allowed too much physical contact against Reese . His comments reflected Atlanta's frustration with the way its leading star was defended. However, the team's offensive struggles went well beyond Reese's performance.

The Valkyries capitalize on Atlanta's mistakes

If this game made one thing clear, it was that the Dream needed much more than a strong individual performance to pull through. Atlanta shot just 29.2% from the field and committed 17 turnovers , numbers that severely limited its chances of staying competitive until the final buzzer.

Rhyne Howard led Atlanta in scoring with 20 points and 5 rebounds. Jordin Canada added 12 points, while Allisha Gray finished with 10, but the offense never found the consistency needed to change the outcome.

Golden State, meanwhile, made the most of its defensive effort. Kiah Stokes contributed 13 points and three blocks, while Veronica Burton also scored 13 points and recorded four blocks. Together, they helped shut down Atlanta's attempts to build momentum and kept the game under control.

The first half ended with the Valkyries leading 25-22 , marking the lowest-scoring halftime in WNBA Finals history, according to the available game data.

The next game is scheduled for Thursday, October 29, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta . The Dream will have their home crowd behind them, but they will also face enormous pressure: they must win to tie the series and force a decisive Game 7.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s game outdrew Angel Reese’s record-setting WNBA Finals Game 4 by 1.4 million viewers
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark’s regular-season game drew a larger audience than a record-setting WNBA Finals matchup featuring Angel Reese
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s regular-season game drew a larger audience than a record-setting WNBA Finals matchup featuring Angel Reese
articles.body:
A regular-season WNBA game featuring Caitlin Clark’s Indiana Fever drew a larger audience than the record-setting Game 4 of the 2026 Finals . Indiana’s Aug. 23 matchup with the Chicago Sky averaged 3.31 million viewers across NBC and Peacock . Game 4 between Angel Reese’s Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries averaged 1.895 million, a difference of about 1.4 million.

The comparison is especially striking because both figures use NBC and Peacock’s combined Total Audience Delivery measurement. But the games had different stakes and time slots: Fever-Sky aired in prime time, while Finals Game 4 tipped off at 1 p.m. ET. The Finals broadcast still set a record for the most-watched Game 4 in WNBA Finals history.

Clark’s game topped the record-setting Finals audience

The Fever-Sky matchup was the most-watched regular-season WNBA game since the league’s opening weekend in 1997 and the third-most-watched WNBA game ever. Clark scored 37 points in Indiana’s 113-90 win. Reese was not in that game: she had joined Atlanta after being traded by Chicago earlier in the year, so the Fever were facing her former team.

Clark and Reese did meet on the court earlier that month. On Aug. 16, the Fever beat the Dream 95-91 in overtime, and that game averaged 2.58 million viewers on ESPN, setting a cable record for a WNBA game. Clark finished with 26 points and nine assists; Reese had 15 points and 14 rebounds.

The 1.895 million audience for Finals Game 4 remains a milestone for that round of the championship series , and it peaked at 2.5 million during the finish. The comparison with Fever-Sky shows how a regular-season game involving Clark and her former rival’s old team could draw an even larger audience, even against a Finals matchup featuring Reese.

Since the viewership record was set, the series has moved on: Golden State beat Atlanta 64-55 in Game 5 and now leads the best-of-seven Finals 3-2. Game 6 is Thursday, Oct. 29, at 12:30 p.m. ET (9:30 a.m. PT) in Atlanta, where the Dream will try to keep their season alive. In the United States, the game will air on USA Network and stream on Peacock.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark 'forgets' about her Nike sneakers and makes a new announcement with a special request
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark is turning her attention to a new project away from the basketball court, asking fans to support her upcoming children's book as she continues to build her profile beyond the WNBA
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark is turning her attention to a new project away from the basketball court, asking fans to support her upcoming children's book as she continues to build her profile beyond the WNBA
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark has another big announcement for her fans, but this time it has nothing to do with basketball or her new Nike signature sneakers.

The Indiana Fever star is preparing to release her first children's picture book, and she has issued a special request to supporters ahead of its arrival.

The book, titled EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams, is scheduled to be published by Random House Books for Young Readers on Tuesday, November 3. With the release date approaching, Clark has encouraged her followers to pre-order a copy online.

“BIG NEWS! I wrote a picture book,” Clark wrote on Instagram in May. “Illustrated by @adriillustration. Available wherever books are sold on November 3rd, 2026! Pre-order your copy from @randomhousekids at the link in their bio.”

Her latest appeal was more direct, with Clark using her Instagram Story to remind fans about the upcoming release.

“Pre-order your copy from @randomhousekids at the link in their bio,” Clark wrote on her Instagram story.

The announcement highlights another side of the basketball star's growing career. While her performances with Indiana have helped establish her as one of the WNBA's biggest names, Clark is also developing projects that reach audiences beyond the sport.

Clark's book shares a message about teamwork and chasing dreams

The picture book is written in rhyming verse and explores how relationships, encouragement and perseverance contribute to achieving ambitions. Rather than focusing solely on individual success, its message centres on the importance of family, friends and teammates.

Illustrated by Adriana Predoi , the book is intended for young readers and reflects themes that have also featured throughout Clark's basketball journey.

The publisher describes it as a story about finding the extraordinary in everyday life and recognising the people who help make personal achievements possible.

The project also connects with Clark's work supporting younger generations. Through the Caitlin Clark Foundation, she has backed initiatives involving youth sports, education and nutrition.

A children's book gives her another opportunity to share a positive message with young fans who look up to her.

The timing is notable because Clark has also recently reached a major milestone in her relationship with Nike. Her first signature basketball shoe, the Caitlin 1, became available globally on October 1, marking a significant step in her commercial career.

The collection was developed around her playing style and includes apparel alongside the footwear.

Although the new sneakers have attracted considerable attention, Clark's latest social media message is focused on encouraging fans to support her literary debut.

The two projects demonstrate how her influence is expanding into different areas, from sportswear to children's publishing.

A strong season for Clark despite Indiana's playoff disappointment

Clark's off-court projects arrive after an impressive individual campaign with the Fever. Indiana finished the 2026 regular season with a 28-16 record and the sixth seed in the playoffs, but its postseason ended in a first-round series defeat against the Las Vegas Aces .

Clark nevertheless delivered strong numbers, averaging 22.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 8.3 assists across 40 regular-season appearances.

She was subsequently named to the Associated Press All-WNBA First Team, alongside teammate Kelsey Mitchell , following a season in which she ranked among the league's leading scorers and playmakers.

The campaign represented an important response after Clark missed much of the previous season through injury. Her return to form helped keep Indiana competitive, even though the team fell short of its postseason ambitions.

Now that the Fever's season is over, Clark has more time to focus on her activities away from the court. She has previously participated in golf events, including The Annika Pro-Am, while maintaining partnerships with major brands such as Nike, Gatorade and State Farm.

With EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams arriving on November 3, Clark's latest request gives supporters a new way to engage with her work.

For a player known for her impact on basketball, the book offers a different platform for sharing the values of teamwork, persistence and ambition with the next generation.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham's future with Caitlin Clark could abruptly end as Fever shakeup unfolds
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever could be making wholesale roster changes heading into the 2027 season.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever could be making wholesale roster changes heading into the 2027 season.
articles.body:
They didn't quite take the quantum leap many analysts envisioned, but the Indiana Fever had a very solid season in 2026. They finished 28-16 and second in the Eastern Conference , but they just so happened to run into WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs.

Still, there were plenty of positive signs for the future. Caitlin Clark took another step in her superstar development, while Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston were their usual impactful selves. No one else truly stood out, though. Sophie Cunningham played the fourth-most minutes per game for the team, but she fully accepted a bench role.

Cunningham played in 43 games, but started just three of them. Practically all of her numbers, including minutes per game, went down from the 2025 season. With that in mind, and a major shakeup in the organization's front office, there are real questions about whether Cunningham will continue with the team .

Sophie Cunningham breaks silence on Indiana Fever front office upheaval

Cunningham finally broke her silence on the front office upheaval, speaking about team president Kelly Krauskopf resigning and general manager Amber Cox being fired. In her comments, Cunningham sounded almost as if she has already put the Fever in the rearview mirror.

​There was not a lot of warning, and that’s okay. I think that’s probably a good thing that you kind of keep it in-house a little bit. But you know what? Kelly and Amber, they’re phenomenal, phenomenal people. They cared a lot about us as players and as individuals outside the court. And so I have nothing but great things to say about them. Hopefully the Fever come in and bring people who can do a really good job for that program. I was blessed to be under Kelly and Amber, and I hope them the very best, and so we’ll see what happens.

Instead of saying "we", Cunningham opted to speak about the Fever in third person . It appears likely that Cunningham could test the free agency waters, which would lead to Clark losing her enforcer and a very good friend within the locker room.

articles.title: New Indiana Fever GM faces major challenge: Most important decision involves Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell, and Aliyah Boston
articles.standfirst: The franchise's next executive inherits a complicated salary-cap situation as three established stars shape its championship ambitions
articles.summary: The franchise's next executive inherits a complicated salary-cap situation as three established stars shape its championship ambitions
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever have spent several seasons building a roster capable of challenging the WNBA 's established contenders. Now, with three star players commanding increasingly significant contracts, the franchise faces the difficult task of preserving what it has created.

Indiana's search for a new general manager comes at a particularly important moment, following a 2026 campaign that demonstrated both the team's championship potential and its limitations.

Led by Caitlin Clark , Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston , the Fever averaged a league-leading 96 points per game. However, defensive shortcomings proved costly during their first-round playoff elimination against the Las Vegas Aces .

The incoming executive must therefore make difficult financial decisions while finding reinforcements capable of turning Indiana into a more balanced contender.

Clark 's long-term future represents one of the most significant decisions awaiting the new general manager, although the star guard has already indicated that winning remains her priority.

The 24-year-old is eligible for an Exceptional Performance Initial Contract extension, potentially placing her among the WNBA's highest-paid players.

However, Clark suggested during her October 8 exit interview that she would consider the wider implications of her contract before making a decision.

"I just want to do what's best for the team and make sure we have the opportunity to be able to win championships," Clark said.

"My focus is on winning. I certainly know what I deserve and what I'm worth, but at the same time, sometimes you have to make sacrifices."

Clark also emphasized her commitment to remaining with the franchise, stating: "No matter what, I'm going to be here."

Her position could provide Indiana with valuable flexibility as it attempts to accommodate several major contracts.

Mitchell's free agency presents immediate challenge

While Clark 's future appears relatively secure, Mitchell 's situation requires a more immediate decision.

The veteran guard is approaching unrestricted free agency after earning approximately $1.4 million in 2026, with another substantial contract potentially awaiting her.

Retaining Mitchell would preserve one of the league's most productive backcourts, but Indiana must also account for Boston's four-year, $6.3 million extension.

IndyStar reporter Chloe Peterson believes managing those competing financial commitments should be the incoming executive's central responsibility.

"Indiana's new GM should be someone who can, above all, navigate this salary cap situation they're in," Peterson said.

"They're running out of space already. This new GM needs to figure out how to make it all work, either through trades, the draft, or smart free agency moves, including if they themselves want to retain Mitchell for 2027."

Pressure to build championship-winning defense

Financial planning represents only part of the challenge awaiting Cox 's replacement.

Indiana must also strengthen its defense without sacrificing the offensive chemistry that has made the team so competitive.

Peterson warned that the next general manager will need to handle intense public attention surrounding the franchise.

"The new GM also needs to have a form of thick skin," she said. "There is a microscope around the Fever, especially, and that comes with more fans, detractors, and trolls."

Pacers Sports & Entertainment is overseeing the search, with a new appointment expected before January's free-agency period.

The Fever already possess the foundation of a potential championship team. Their next general manager must determine how to protect that core while addressing the weaknesses that have prevented Indiana from taking the final step.

articles.title: Angel Reese struggles before Game 6 of WNBA Finals, as Sophie Cunningham outplays her on off-court
articles.standfirst: The Dream forward faces crucial championship test after an off-court ranking revealed Cunningham's narrow advantage
articles.summary: The Dream forward faces crucial championship test after an off-court ranking revealed Cunningham's narrow advantage
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are preparing for a must-win WNBA Finals showdown against the Golden State Valkyries , but Angel Reese has found herself on the losing side of an unexpected comparison with Sophie Cunningham .

Reese has been instrumental in Atlanta's championship pursuit, averaging 17.0 points and 10.6 rebounds during the postseason after leading the WNBA in rebounding throughout the regular season.

Her performances have strengthened an already impressive profile beyond basketball, where major sponsorship agreements and millions of social media followers have established her among the league's biggest commercial attractions.

However, Cunningham has emerged ahead of the Dream forward in SportsPro's reported ranking of the 50 most marketable athletes of 2026, despite Reese's continued success on and off the court.

The Indiana Fever guard received an overall score of 65.34 out of 100, narrowly exceeding Reese 's 64.28 and securing 28th place in the assessment.

Why Cunningham ranked ahead of Reese

The results reflect a broader measurement of commercial influence rather than an evaluation of basketball ability, with SportsPro examining established brand value, recent momentum and future commercial potential.

Cunningham 's advantage came primarily from her growing visibility since joining Indiana in 2025, where her outspoken personality and close association with Caitlin Clark have significantly expanded her audience.

The veteran guard has built an Instagram following of approximately 4.3 million while securing partnerships with Adidas, Arby's, Marriott Bonvoy and Quest Nutrition.

Her commercial momentum score of 34.85 considerably exceeded Reese 's 18.49, helping explain why Cunningham finished ahead despite trailing in other categories.

Reese , however, recorded stronger results for established brand value, earning 31.52 compared with Cunningham 's 24.76.

The Atlanta star also led in projected commercial growth, scoring 14.27 against Cunningham 's 5.73.

Those figures suggest the overall result was influenced more by Cunningham 's recent rise than by any decline in Reese 's established commercial appeal.

Reese retains advantage in sponsorship potential

Reese has continued expanding her commercial portfolio through partnerships with Reebok, Barbie, Victoria's Secret and Reese's, demonstrating her appeal across fashion, lifestyle and sports markets.

Her Instagram audience of approximately 5.3 million also remains larger than Cunningham 's, providing another indication of the different ways athletes can build their influence.

While Cunningham has benefited from the intense attention surrounding Indiana, Reese 's success has developed alongside her individual basketball achievements and growing presence in mainstream entertainment.

Both players have therefore established valuable commercial identities, even if their respective careers have followed different paths.

WNBA Finals provide Reese with immediate opportunity

Reese 's more pressing concern is now Atlanta's attempt to keep its championship hopes alive against Golden State.

The Dream trail the Valkyries 3-2 in the best-of-seven series following a 64-55 defeat in Game 5 on Monday, leaving them needing consecutive victories to secure the franchise's first championship.

Game 6 takes place Thursday, October 29, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, with tipoff scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET.

Another strong postseason performance would give Reese an opportunity to reinforce her standing as one of the WNBA's leading stars.

Although Cunningham holds a narrow advantage in the latest marketability comparison, Reese still has the chance to finish her season with an achievement that would carry significance far beyond commercial rankings.

articles.title: WNBA Finals Chaos: Atlanta Dream unload on league for forcing midday Thursday tipoff
articles.standfirst: Atlanta's ownership group has publicly challenged league officials after a scheduling conflict disrupted its biggest home game
articles.summary: Atlanta's ownership group has publicly challenged league officials after a scheduling conflict disrupted its biggest home game
articles.body:
A championship series should represent the biggest opportunity for a WNBA franchise to showcase its success, but the Atlanta Dream believe the league's handling of the Finals has made that unnecessarily difficult.

Atlanta will host the Golden State Valkyries in Game 6 on Thursday, October 29, with tipoff scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET, an unusual time for a championship contest that could determine the destination of the title.

The afternoon start allows the Dream to play at State Farm Arena, where the Atlanta Hawks are also scheduled to face the Cleveland Cavaliers later that evening.

However, the arrangement has angered Atlanta's ownership group, which insists the scheduling problem could have been addressed long before the Finals began.

In an open letter to supporters, owners Larry and Robyn Gottesdiener , Suzanne Abair and Renee Montgomery accused WNBA leadership of failing to give their concerns sufficient attention.

The ownership group explained that potential conflicts were identified when the league confirmed its postseason schedule, with State Farm Arena already committed to hosting NBA games.

"Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena," the owners wrote.

"As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns. Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

Their frustration extends beyond the inconvenience of an afternoon game, with Atlanta questioning whether the possibility of the Dream reaching the championship series had received adequate consideration.

"Perhaps it was assumed that the Dream would not make it this far. Perhaps our place in the Finals was not accounted for," the letter continued.

"Whatever the reason, the reality is that we are here. We earned our place in the Finals, and our city deserves the opportunity to show up for it's team."

Why Atlanta Dream accepted controversial start time

The alternative would likely have involved returning to Gateway Center Arena , Atlanta's regular-season home, which accommodates approximately 3,500 spectators.

State Farm Arena offers capacity for around 17,000 fans, making it a considerably more attractive option for a franchise competing for its first WNBA championship.

The Hawks agreed to move their game against Cleveland to 8 p.m. ET, creating enough time for the Dream to stage their Finals contest earlier in the day.

Atlanta's owners praised their NBA counterparts for accommodating the arrangement but maintained that Thursday's start time was far from ideal.

"Playing a midday game on a Thursday is not what we would have chosen and not what we fought for," they wrote.

Atlanta Dream demand greater respect

The scheduling dispute comes with Golden State holding a 3-2 advantage in the best-of-seven series following consecutive victories.

Atlanta must win Game 6 to force a deciding contest, while the Valkyries can secure the championship with another victory.

The Dream 's owners believe their postseason success demonstrates why the franchise deserves greater consideration when major league decisions are made.

"This incredible run by our players has also made something else abundantly clear: The Atlanta Dream has earned the right to be taken seriously," their letter stated.

They concluded by emphasizing that the franchise expects future planning to reflect its competitive standing.

Adding: "We intend to keep building. We intend to keep winning. And we expect the opportunities, planning, and consideration afforded to us to reflect the level at which we compete."
