articles.title: Caitlin Clark surprises Indiana high school girls’ basketball team with her Nike Caitlin 1s in their locker room
articles.standfirst: The Zionsville girls got a locker-room surprise they won’t soon forget
articles.summary: The Zionsville girls got a locker-room surprise they won’t soon forget
articles.body:
Boxes of blue Nike Caitlin 1s arrived for the Zionsville Community High School girls’ basketball team, and the players’ reaction was immediate : screams, hugs, jumping and smiles as they opened their new sneakers. The team shared a video of the unboxing on X and thanked both Nike and Caitlin Clark.

The moment offered a glimpse of what Clark’s signature shoe means to young players in Indiana. For the team, the Caitlin 1s weren’t just another pair of basketball sneakers. They came from the state’s biggest basketball star and carried the details of a shoe built around her game.

The Caitlin 1s were designed around Clark’s speed and range

Nike released Clark’s first signature shoe globally on Oct. 1, with two launch colorways: Caitlin Blue and Warning Code Yellow. Adult pairs retailed for $140. The design includes a lightweight Nike Opticast upper, a responsive Air Zoom Turbo unit in the forefoot and Cushlon foam for cushioning and control.

The personal touches connect the shoe to Clark’s identity and playing style. Its upper features her “CC” logo and references to her No. 22, while the outsole carries messages including “Shoot More Threes” and “From Anywhere.” Nike says the design was developed around the quick first step, step-back and shot release Clark wanted to support.

The Caitlin 1 launch quickly became a major moment for Nike. CNBC reported that the shoes nearly sold out on Nike.com within two hours of their U.S. debut, with only sizes above 15 left about an hour after they went on sale.

Nike CEO Elliott Hill later called it the company’s largest women’s signature shoe launch and said it was available in 5,000 stores twice the average for a Nike Basketball signature release.

Clark’s Indiana Fever teammates had received blue pairs before the public launch. She gave them the unreleased shoes after returning from the U.S. women’s basketball team’s gold-medal run at the FIBA Women’s World Cup.

The Zionsville gift carried that same excitement to a group of young Indiana players, who got to experience the Caitlin 1 as fans and hoopers.

For Nike, the Zionsville unboxing was the kind of product showcase a polished ad can’t quite reproduce : a locker room full of young athletes celebrating a shoe they were eager to wear. Their post thanked both the brand and Clark, but the players’ joy did the talking.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham still afraid: She reveals 20 different stalkers are being monitored by the FBI
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star has revealed disturbing concerns about her safety while discussing an ongoing stalking case
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star has revealed disturbing concerns about her safety while discussing an ongoing stalking case
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has become one of the most recognizable personalities in women's basketball, but the Indiana Fever guard says the increased attention has brought serious concerns about her personal safety.

The 30-year-old made a startling disclosure during an appearance on Theo Von's This Past Weekend podcast, explaining that she believes the FBI is monitoring approximately 20 individuals because of their behavior toward her.

Her comments came amid an ongoing criminal case involving Kevin Singh , an Indiana man accused of repeatedly contacting Cunningham through threatening and sexually explicit social media messages.

Although Cunningham has embraced the WNBA's expanding audience, she acknowledged that greater visibility has also exposed players to troubling situations away from basketball.

"The more you're visible on TV, you're gonna get more fans. Like, people are gonna know who you are, and that's a really great thing," Cunningham explained.

"But there's also a lot of like, kind of crazy people too that like, we do have a lot of stalkers. I know I do."

When Von asked whether she had personally experienced stalking, Cunningham suggested the situation was considerably more extensive than many supporters might realize.

"Oh my gosh. Yeah. Like, I will have to check if I'm even allowed to say this, but like, I like have, I think, 20, I think, people kind of that the FBI are watching for me, me alone," she said.

Cunningham declined to identify those individuals, explaining that she wasn't permitted to discuss their identities publicly. However, one case involving Cunningham has already resulted in criminal charges and remains before the courts.

Judge rejects alleged stalker's request

Singh , 49, has been held in Marion County Jail since his June 23 arrest on charges of stalking, intimidation and harassment.

His attorney recently requested a reduction of his $40,000 bail, arguing that Singh had been assaulted while in custody and needed to leave jail for his safety.

A Marion County judge rejected the request on October 23 after court records failed to substantiate the alleged assault.

Cunningham learned about the ruling during her podcast appearance and immediately welcomed the decision.

"Nice," she said while clapping. "Good work, judge."

According to investigators, Singh allegedly continued contacting Cunningham after receiving a cease-and-desist letter in April.

Court documents also describe an earlier delivery to Gainbridge Fieldhouse containing a letter and a cologne-sprayed Guns N' Roses T-shirt.

Singh has not been convicted of the charges involving Cunningham.

Indiana Fever star described feeling unsafe

The allegations have already affected Cunningham 's daily life, according to statements recorded by investigators.

A detective wrote that Cunningham had been spending more time at home, experiencing nightmares and feeling constantly concerned about her surroundings.

The case follows a separate stalking prosecution involving Fever teammate Caitlin Clark , whose harasser was sentenced to prison in 2025.

Cunningham 's revelations also arrive as she approaches unrestricted free agency following Indiana's playoff elimination against the Las Vegas Aces .

While her future with the Fever remains uncertain, the guard's latest comments highlight a growing challenge facing high-profile athletes: protecting their personal safety while navigating the increasing visibility of professional women's sports.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham enters the WNBA anthem controversy and explains why she remains on the court
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player spoke about the decision by some teams to leave before the national anthem and explained why she chooses to stay.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player spoke about the decision by some teams to leave before the national anthem and explained why she chooses to stay.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham spoke openly about one of the issues that occasionally sparks debate around the WNBA. During her appearance on the podcast This Past Weekend, hosted by Theo Von, the Indiana Fever player explained why she chooses to remain on the court during the United States national anthem.

The topic came up when Von asked her about the decision by some players or teams to leave the court before the anthem begins to be performed. Cunningham explained that this practice is not new and took the opportunity to clarify why she prefers to stay.

Cunningham explains what the anthem means to her

The guard linked her decision to her family history and the respect she feels for those who have served in the Armed Forces.

Cunningham said that she has family members who have served in the military and highlighted the sacrifices that, from her perspective, military personnel and veterans make to protect the freedoms enjoyed by American citizens.

“Personally, I am grateful and support the people who serve. We have family members who have served, and they do things that are unimaginable to us so that we can be here living our dreams and having the freedoms that we have”

The player also made it clear that her decision is personal and that she does not intend for her teammates to necessarily share her stance.

I am going to show my support and my affection. That is my stance. That does not mean that everyone has to think the same way, or that it is right or wrong. I am very proud of where I come from, and I am proud to be a U.S. citizen.

A personal decision, not a criticism of her teammates

The conversation once again brought to the forefront a question that has accompanied the WNBA over the last few years: the way some players express their positions on social and political issues, including during the national anthem.

Cunningham, however, avoided framing her decision as a criticism of those who act differently.

The Indiana player made her position clear without presenting her choice as the only correct way to approach the moment before the games.

The Indiana player made her position clear without presenting her choice as the only correct way to approach the moment before the games.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark gets up close and personal with LeBron James and earns praise from Tyrese Maxey
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star was present for the Philadelphia 76ers game on Wednesday night.
articles.summary: The WNBA star was present for the Philadelphia 76ers game on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Wednesday night's game between the Philadelphia 76ers and Indiana Pacers was a special one for a couple of reasons. Of course, it was LeBron James ' first visit to Indianapolis as a member of the Sixers. There was also a special guest in the building: Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark .

The WNBA star couldn't pass up the opportunity to watch The King and co. in her home arena, Gainbridge Fieldhouse . Clark sat as close as possible to the action and even whipped out an old school camera to snap pics of James and the rest of the stars on the court .

Once the game concluded, Clark had a special, personal moment with James . The two met up in the hallways within the stadium, and James even came bearing a gift for Clark. She was clearly starstruck by James, as anyone would be.

Tyrese Maxey had to hold himself back from fanning out over Caitlin Clark

While Clark was starstruck by James, 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey was actually starstruck by Clark herself. Maxey spoke about Clark following the game to the media and had nothing but praise for the Fever player .

I think that was my first time really meeting her. Honestly that's just like, shoot, another person I like to watch. She's cold. She's nice. Seeing her today was really cool. Sometimes you try not to fan out, but it was really cool seeing her. This is her building, she plays here too... So it was good seeing her. She's nice.

It was a special night for Clark and for the Sixers players who got to meet her. It would have been nice if her close friend, Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton , could play in the game, but he's dealing with a hamstring injury at the moment.

articles.title: Angel Reese means business in all-black outfit with touch of gold before Game 6 of WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: Reese looked very serious as she entered State Farm Arena ahead of a must-win game for the Atlanta Dream.
articles.summary: Reese looked very serious as she entered State Farm Arena ahead of a must-win game for the Atlanta Dream.
articles.body:
While the start time of 12:30pm ET on a Thursday has been extremely polarizing, Game 6 of the WNBA Finals went ahead anyway. It's a must-win game for the Atlanta Dream , who are down 3-2 in the series to the Golden State Valkyries .

The Dream have had offensive struggles, which has naturally led to criticism for star forward Angel Reese , who hasn't been efficient on the offensive end. Reese and co. know it was all business heading into Game 6, and Reese's outfit while arriving to the arena made that clear .

Reese pulled up to her home stadium, State Farm Arena , in a nearly all-black outfit, with hints of gold sprinkled throughout . Reese sported black shades and black and gold high heels. She was ready to go to work from the get-go.

That attitude worked out to get the Dream started off on the right foot, as they dominated the first quarter 32-15 at home . Reese, in particular, came out with a ton of energy on the court - even celebrating a tough bucket in front of the Valkyrie bench at one point.

articles.title: Indiana Fever puts Caitlin Clark in charge of the search for a new general manager
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever have hired Excel Search & Advisory to help identify their next general manager, giving Caitlin Clark a potential voice in the franchise's future as the organization prepares for a crucial offseason
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever have hired Excel Search & Advisory to help identify their next general manager, giving Caitlin Clark a potential voice in the franchise's future as the organization prepares for a crucial offseason
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever are turning to an unexpected connection as they search for a new general manager: the agency that represents Caitlin Clark .

Following a major front-office shake-up, Indiana has hired Excel Search & Advisory to assist with the recruitment process.

The firm is owned by Excel Sports Management, which represents Clark , creating a notable link between the franchise's biggest star and the search for its next basketball operations leader.

However, Clark will not make the final hiring decision. That responsibility remains with Pacers Sports & Entertainment, with players expected to have input into the process.

The search follows the departures of team president Kelly Krauskopf and general manager Amber Cox on October 23. The changes leave Indiana facing important decisions about its roster, salary commitments and championship ambitions ahead of the 2027 season.

Clark has already made clear that she wants to help shape the team's future. During her end-of-season interview, the guard explained that she and fellow star Aliyah Boston intended to play an active role in recruiting players.

“That’s the responsibility of me and AB at this point as the leaders of this team,” Clark said in her exit interview.

“Then, obviously, if we get Kelsey back, she could be helping us as well. Us and Amber always have an open dialogue about players. At the end of the day, Amber is the GM and she makes final call but she certainly asks us our opinion and wants us to have a voice in that.

“(I want to) continue to use my voice in that the best I can and continue to help free agents who wanna come here and show them around if they wanna visit.”

A critical offseason for Clark and the Fever

Excel's appointment gives the Fever access to a firm with experience in sports executive recruitment. It has worked on searches involving teams and organizations across women's basketball and other sports, and is also assisting with the search for the WNBA's next commissioner.

The connection to Clark is noteworthy, but it does not automatically mean the star guard controls the appointment.

The ownership group will retain the final say, while Clark and Boston are expected to provide their perspectives on the players and leadership they believe can help Indiana compete.

According to The Indianapolis Star, there is no fixed deadline for the appointment, although the start of free agency in January 2027 means the organization cannot afford to delay its planning for long.

The next GM inherits a complicated roster

The incoming executive will have several major decisions to make, starting with Kelsey Mitchell' s future. Mitchell is an unrestricted free agent after an outstanding season alongside Clark, and keeping the All-Star guard could be central to Indiana's plans.

Sophie Cunningham is also approaching free agency, adding further uncertainty to the roster. The new GM must balance retaining important contributors with addressing the team's defensive shortcomings.

Indiana finished the 2026 regular season with a franchise-record 28 wins, but its campaign ended against the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs. Despite the team's offensive production, the early exit demonstrated that scoring alone will not be enough to deliver a championship.

The franchise also faces significant financial considerations. Boston has already secured an extension, while Clark's own contract situation will be an important part of Indiana's long-term planning.

The new executive will need to understand the salary cap and determine how to build a balanced roster around the team's young stars.

Meanwhile, Pacers Sports & Entertainment CEO Mel Raines will oversee business operations, with the organization not planning to fill Krauskopf's vacant team president position at this stage.

Clark's involvement could help Indiana understand what its leading players need to succeed, but the real test will be finding an executive who can turn those ambitions into a championship-caliber team.

With free agency approaching and key players facing uncertain futures, the Fever's next appointment could shape the franchise for years to come.

articles.title: Allisha Gray Erupts, Angel Reese Grinds: Atlanta Stuns Valkyries to Force Game 7
articles.standfirst: Faced with elimination, the Dream’s star duo delivers under pressure, shifting all the momentum heading into the ultimate showdown
articles.summary: Faced with elimination, the Dream’s star duo delivers under pressure, shifting all the momentum heading into the ultimate showdown
articles.body:
A llisha Gray scored 23 points and Rhyne Howard had 21 as the hot-shooting Atlanta Dream held off Golden State's late rally to take an 80-69 victory over the Valkyries in Game 6 on Thursday to pull even in the WNBA Finals .

The decisive Game 7 will be played at Golden State on Saturday night as each team seeks its first WNBA championship.

After having their lowest scoring games of the Finals in losses in Games 4 and 5, the Dream enjoyed an offensive awakening when faced with the must-win mandate. Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 26 points. Tiffany Hayes added 15.

Atlanta’s biggest lead was 25 points. The Valkyries stormed back in the final minutes, pulling to 77-66 on Laeticia Amihere ’s two free throws with 1:57 remaining. After being held to 22 points in the first half of their 65-55 loss in Game 5, the Dream matched that total in the first 6:30 of the opening quarter.

Much of the production came on 3s. Atlanta made 6 of 8 3s and 11 of 15 shots overall while racing to a 32-15 lead in the first quarter.

After leading 6-5, the Dream pulled away with 13 unanswered points in a run that included two 3s from Jordin Canada . Reese joined the 3-point party with a shot from the corner in the second period. Entering the game, the Dream were 15-0 when Reese had at least one 3.

While Atlanta’s sharp shooting continued for a 46-26 halftime lead, the Valkyries struggled. Golden State made only 9 of 34 shots in the half , often struggling to create open opportunities because of the Dream’s smothering defense.

Howard opened the second half with another 3-pointer. Valkyries guard Veronica Burton was called for a flagrant foul later midway through the third period when an officials’ review determined she made an unnecessary windup and contact on Howard’s face as Howard was driving for a basket.

Kaila Charles closed the third quarter with a 3-pointer for Golden State that trimmed Atlanta’s lead to 16 points at 63-47. It was the smallest lead for the Dream since the 13-0 run in the opening period.

Golden State pulled to within 13 points at 68-55 before Gray and Reese sank 3s to push the lead to 74-55. Williams’ three-point play cut the led to 77-69 before Gray sank a crucial 3-pointer for Atlanta.

Hayes was called for her fifth foul in a collision for a loose ball with 5:01 remaining. Hayes left the court slowly after receiving attention from a trainer.

articles.title: Angel Reese sets Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on fire with a cheeky taunt to the Golden State bench
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star sparked a fresh social media debate after celebrating an early and-one against the Golden State Valkyries, as her team's season hung in the balance
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star sparked a fresh social media debate after celebrating an early and-one against the Golden State Valkyries, as her team's season hung in the balance
articles.body:
Angel Reese wasted little time making her presence felt during Game 6 of the WNBA Finals, turning an early basket into another talking point about her outspoken approach to basketball.

The Atlanta Dream forward scored through contact and drew a foul in the opening quarter against the Golden State Valkyries before turning toward the opposing bench to make sure her opponents noticed.

The exchange quickly attracted attention online, with fans divided over whether Reese's confidence added excitement to the occasion or crossed the line into unnecessary taunting.

The moment came at a critical point in the series. Atlanta entered Thursday's game trailing 3-2 and facing elimination, with Golden State just one victory away from securing its first WNBA championship.

Reese's energy matched the urgency of the situation. The Dream started aggressively at State Farm Arena, building a commanding first-quarter advantage as their season was on the line.

The forward's interaction with the Valkyries bench became a talking point beyond the game itself, with social media users debating her conduct and whether officials should have intervened.

One fan wrote: "Should be a tech for taunting. Act like you've been there before."

Another joked about the reaction from Golden State's sideline: "Valks bench filing a noise complaint 💀"

Others were less impressed with Reese's approach. "That immature taunting is the one part of Reese's game that comes back to bite her," another fan commented.

The criticism reflected a familiar debate around Reese , whose competitive personality and willingness to engage opponents have become part of her public image.

Reese's attitude divides WNBA fans once again

The reactions continued as fans questioned whether the Dream star's celebrations were appropriate for a player competing on the sport's biggest stage.

" Reese talking to the Valks bench at lunch on a Thursday, bro," one fan commented.

Another wrote: "She’s crying when they’re losing, talking when they’re up huge; at least she's consistent in never shutting up."

A further reaction took aim at the frequency of Reese's celebrations: "When doesn't she let the other team hear it? They could be down by 50, she could be shooting 1 for 30, makes one and she'll flex," another fan said.

The contrasting responses highlight how Reese's style can generate attention even when the wider game carries much greater consequences.

Supporters often view her intensity as part of what makes her an entertaining competitor, while critics argue that the celebrations can distract from her team's performance.

It was not the first time Reese had drawn attention for exchanging words with Golden State during the Finals. Her earlier interactions with the Valkyries bench and individual players had already become viral moments during the series.

Atlanta keeps its championship hopes alive

Beyond the social media debate, Reese delivered a significant performance when Atlanta needed one. The Dream defeated Golden State 80-69, forcing a decisive Game 7 after trailing 3-2 in the series.

Reese finished with 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists, while Allisha Gray scored 23 points and Rhyne Howard added 21.

Atlanta's strong start helped establish control, although Golden State fought back in the second half and threatened to reduce the deficit. The Dream ultimately held on to keep their championship hopes alive.

The result means the teams will meet again on Saturday, October 31, with the WNBA title at stake. It will be the first Game 7 in Finals history, adding even more significance to an already heated matchup.

For Reese , Thursday's performance provided an important response after Atlanta's recent losses. Her exchange with the Valkyries bench may have dominated online discussion, but her contribution on the court helped ensure the season would continue.

Now, with everything to play for in Game 7, the spotlight will remain on Reese and whether her trademark confidence can help Atlanta complete its comeback.

articles.title: Angel Reese hits a celebration dance with Usher after making WNBA history
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star is turning doubters into believers while bringing some of the biggest names in entertainment courtside
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star is turning doubters into believers while bringing some of the biggest names in entertainment courtside
articles.body:
A ngel Reese had a challenging start to her professional WNBA career, becoming one of the most questioned players in the league . One of the main criticisms against her was that she constantly promoted herself as one of the driving forces behind women's basketball's generational shift, taking credit for part of the WNBA's growth and the increased attention surrounding the sport.

Her confidence in speaking about her own impact earned her plenty of backlash on social media , where many fans disagreed with her perspective and constantly compared her to Caitlin Clark. While some questioned Reese's level of play, others praised the Indiana Fever star and used the comparison to discredit the Atlanta player's performances.

The criticism grew stronger when Reese began making a name for herself in the fashion and entertainment industries . Some fans believed she was dividing her attention between too many projects, especially since her results on the court did not always match the expectations she had created. However, her arrival in Atlanta has marked a major turning point in her career.

Reese is changing the narrative on the court

Angel Reese is not only competing in the WNBA Finals but has also become a key piece of her team's success. Her performances have increased her importance on the court, with some experts considering this the best basketball of her career. Now, she has the opportunity to become a league champion, potentially getting the last laugh over some of the players she was previously compared to, including Caitlin Clark.

It is also encouraging to see more celebrities gathering to watch her play and support the growth of women's basketball. The presence of stars such as Usher in the arenas highlights the reach the WNBA is gaining and helps bring greater exposure and commercial opportunities to women's sports. That growing interest could also help improve conditions for female athletes and bring their opportunities closer to those enjoyed by men.

Usher joins Reese in a viral celebration

Celebrities are not just attending games; they are also joining players in their celebrations. Usher, who has supported women's basketball for years, became part of one of the most talked-about moments after Atlanta defeated the Golden State Valkyries in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals.

The 24-year-old star ran toward the R&B singer to hug him as he waited for her with a big smile in the tunnels of State Farm Arena. In the video, Reese also invites Usher into the locker room to meet her teammates, turning the moment into a celebration that quickly went viral on social media.

The WNBA Finals become a celebrity gathering

Usher was not the only familiar face in attendance for Game 6. Musicians T-Pain and T.I. were also spotted supporting the players, while Boosie Badazz surprised fans with an impromptu performance of his hit Wipe Me Down.

Celebrity appearances have been a constant throughout the Finals, with other notable figures including Kerry Washington, rapper Latto, Zendaya, Gunna, Megan Rapinoe, 2 Chainz and 21 Savage, among others. Their presence reflects the growing interest in the competition and the place women's basketball is earning within the sports entertainment industry.

Her performances have increased her importance on the court, with some experts considering this the best basketball of her career. Now, she has the opportunity to become a league champion, potentially getting the last laugh over some of the players she was previously compared to, including Caitlin Clark.

It is also encouraging to see more celebrities gathering to watch her play and support the growth of women's basketball. The presence of stars such as Usher in the arenas highlights the reach the WNBA is gaining and helps bring greater exposure and commercial opportunities to women's sports. That growing interest could also help improve conditions for female athletes and bring their opportunities closer to those enjoyed by men.

Celebrities are not just attending games; they are also joining players in their celebrations. Usher, who has supported women's basketball for years, became part of one of the most talked-about moments after Atlanta defeated the Golden State Valkyries in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals.

The 24-year-old star ran toward the R&B singer to hug him as he waited for her with a big smile in the tunnels of State Farm Arena. In the video, Reese also invites Usher into the locker room to meet her teammates, turning the moment into a celebration that quickly went viral on social media.
The WNBA Finals become a celebrity gathering

Usher was not the only familiar face in attendance for Game 6. Musicians T-Pain and T.I. were also spotted supporting the players, while Boosie Badazz surprised fans with an impromptu performance of his hit Wipe Me Down.

Celebrity appearances have been a constant throughout the Finals, with other notable figures including Kerry Washington, rapper Latto, Zendaya, Gunna, Megan Rapinoe, 2 Chainz and 21 Savage, among others. Their presence reflects the growing interest in the competition and the place women's basketball is earning within the sports entertainment industry.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham’s absence from key Fever moment raises questions about her non-negotiable return
articles.standfirst: Another season in Indiana is looking increasingly uncertain for the Fever guard
articles.summary: Another season in Indiana is looking increasingly uncertain for the Fever guard
articles.body:
Indiana Fever fans have been watching closely for any positive news about the team's position on bringing Sophie Cunningham back for a third season. However, the latest signs have not been encouraging for those hoping to see her return to Indianapolis.

Although Cunningham is a controversial figure in the WNBA, she has also become one of the players who attracts the most attention since joining the Fever . Many fans want her back, even as others argue that she does not bring enough to the team and that Indiana would be better off saving the money it would take to offer her another contract.

Cunningham's offseason has been busy, but basketball has been nowhere near the top of her schedule . She has spent time with her family and animals while also revealing several plans for the coming weeks. Her agenda includes traveling to Austin for Formula 1, heading to Los Angeles for a couple of meetings, attending a live taping of Dancing with the Stars with her sister Lindsey, filming another commercial in Phoenix and spending some time working in New York.

A reunion with Caitlin Clark looks less certain

Fans hoping to see Cunningham return have lost some faith as there has been little indication of any connection to Indiana. A recent video has added to those doubts, particularly among those who want to see her reunited with Caitlin Clark. So far, there has been no clear sign of contact between Cunningham and the team.

Her absence has fueled speculation that Cunningham is becoming increasingly distant from Indiana, both on and off the court. It could even point toward a permanent separation, although no decision about her future has been announced.

Indiana is also going through major changes

Cunningham's one-year contract with the Fever has now expired, making her an unrestricted free agent heading into the offseason. Meanwhile, Indiana has already started making changes to its organization, firing general manager Amber Cox just hours after team president Kelly Krauskopf stepped down.

For now, fans will have to wait to see what the next step in Cunningham's career will be and whether she eventually returns to the team where her popularity grew exponentially.

articles.title: Anthem drama: Sophie Cunningham takes a jab at WNBA Finals teams for leaving the court
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard has made her position clear after the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries repeatedly left the floor before the national anthem
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard has made her position clear after the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries repeatedly left the floor before the national anthem
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has weighed into the growing controversy surrounding the national anthem at the WNBA Finals, making it clear that she prefers to remain on the court and show her appreciation for those serving in the United States military.

The Indiana Fever guard discussed the issue during an appearance on comedian Theo Von 's podcast, This Past Weekend, as criticism continued over the pregame routines of the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries .

Both teams have repeatedly left the playing area shortly before "The Star-Spangled Banner" during the championship series, returning once the performance has finished.

Their decision attracted renewed attention during the Finals, with some fans questioning why the players were not present for the national anthem.

When Von asked Cunningham about the situation, she immediately made it clear that her personal views were well established: "You know who you're talking to?"

Cunningham did not directly identify either Finals team or launch an explicit personal attack against individual players.

Instead, she pointed out that the practice had been happening throughout the season and suggested the issue had attracted significantly more attention now that the championship series was underway.

Her own approach, however, is rooted in her family's connection to the military. Cunningham explained that relatives have served and that she feels a responsibility to recognise the sacrifices made by veterans and active-duty personnel.

She said she wants to use opportunities such as the national anthem to show appreciation for those who serve, particularly because their work helps protect the freedoms that allow professional athletes to pursue their careers.

The 30-year-old also acknowledged that people will not necessarily share her perspective, but made no attempt to hide her own sense of national pride: "I take a lot of pride in where I come from and I'm proud to be an American citizen."

WNBA anthem controversy draws political attention

The disagreement has extended well beyond basketball supporters, becoming a talking point in American politics.

Vice President JD Vance criticised the teams' decision, arguing that players should not use the national anthem as an opportunity to express dissatisfaction with political issues.

The debate has also reopened questions about why teams leave the court in the first place. According to the Associated Press, the practice has been common among WNBA franchises for at least six seasons.

Some teams have used the time away from the floor to highlight social justice concerns, while others have treated it as part of their regular pregame preparations.

Golden State has followed the routine since entering the league, while Atlanta has also been doing so for several years. The Valkyries' head coach, Natalie Nakase , has previously described leaving the court as part of the team's established pregame schedule.

Neither team's repeated absence during the Finals should automatically be interpreted as a newly announced political protest.

Cunningham's comments came amid another difficult subject she discussed with Von: the security concerns surrounding her growing public profile.

The Fever guard revealed that she has received threats and experienced stalking, claiming that the FBI is monitoring approximately 20 individuals in connection with concerns about her safety.

One case has already resulted in criminal charges. A 49-year-old Indiana man, Kevin Singh , was arrested in June and accused of stalking and intimidating Cunningham, alongside a separate misdemeanor harassment charge.

According to reporting by the Los Angeles Times, the allegations included repeated messages on social media and a package delivered to the Fever's arena. Singh is facing the charges, which have not been established as convictions.

The situation highlights the more troubling side of the attention that comes with being a prominent professional athlete.

Cunningham has enjoyed an increasingly visible role in the WNBA, but her comments suggest that the attention has also brought personal concerns away from the court.

There is also an important career decision approaching. Cunningham is a pending free agent heading into the offseason, meaning her future with Indiana remains uncertain.

Her next destination could become one of the talking points of the WNBA's offseason, but her appearance on Von's podcast has already ensured that her position in the national anthem debate is firmly on record.

While she stopped short of directly naming the Dream or Valkyries, Cunningham made clear that honouring military personnel and expressing pride in her country remain important parts of her personal values.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Halloween Nike Caitlin 1 “Jinx” turns childhood fear into a glowing story
articles.standfirst: Nike’s video reveals the childhood memory behind the shoe
articles.summary: Nike’s video reveals the childhood memory behind the shoe
articles.body:
Nike Basketball introduces the Halloween shoe with a short, playful message: “Just the Caitlin 1 ‘Jinx.’ Face your fears. Then lace them up.” The video then explains the name. As a kid, Caitlin Clark was terrified of Jinx, her neighbor’s cat. She never forgot the feline and eventually turned that childhood fear into a pair of signature sneakers.

The story gives the Caitlin 1 “Jinx” a personal meaning beyond its Halloween colors. Clark’s childhood nemesis becomes the inspiration for a shoe bearing her name, turning a memory that once frightened her into something she can wear on the court. The video’s final line nods to a cat’s nine lives, giving the reveal a clever finish.

The Caitlin 1 gets a glow-in-the-dark Halloween makeover

The “Jinx” colorway pairs a dark upper with vivid green details. In Nike’s video, the shoe glows along the sole in the dark, while its green accents stand out against the black design. That eerie effect gives the sneaker its Halloween identity without changing the story at its center.

The Caitlin 1’s performance setup includes a Zoom Air Turbo unit in the forefoot, a full-length Cushlon midsole and an Opticast upper.

The forefoot cushioning supports quick, responsive movement, while the shoe’s upper and midsole are designed for the demands of a guard’s game. The “Jinx” edition adds a distinctive look to that same basketball foundation.

Now, that childhood fear inspires a sneaker with a glow-in-the-dark design and a playful message: “Face your fears. Then lace them up.”

Reports have listed the “Jinx” Caitlin 1 for a U.S. release on Oct. 30 at $150, though Nike has not officially confirmed either detail. The standard Caitlin 1 launched at $140.

articles.title: Drama in the WNBA Finals: Veronica Burton is clear about who is to blame for the Valkyries' stumble in Game 6
articles.standfirst: Valkyries star doesn't hold back after Atlanta exposes Golden State's defensive weaknesses
articles.summary: Valkyries star doesn't hold back after Atlanta exposes Golden State's defensive weaknesses
articles.body:
Veronica Burton didn't look for excuses after the Golden State Valkyries let a crucial opportunity slip away in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals.

The guard pointed directly to her team's defensive failures, calling the opening-quarter performance unacceptable after the Atlanta Dream secured an 80-69 victory to force a deciding Game 7.

Golden State entered Thursday's matchup with a 3-2 series advantage after consecutive defensive wins. The Valkyries had limited Atlanta to 62 points in Game 4 and just 55 in Game 5, moving within one victory of the franchise's first championship.

However, everything changed at State Farm Arena, where the Dream delivered an emphatic response.

Atlanta built a commanding 32-15 lead in the opening period, connecting on 11 of its first 15 field-goal attempts, including six three-pointers. The Dream carried a 46-26 advantage into halftime.

Golden State's inability to contain Atlanta from the opening minutes proved particularly disappointing for a team whose identity has been built around defensive discipline.

Burton made clear that responsibility rested with the players rather than the unusual midday start.

“They scored 32 points in the first quarter. That’s unacceptable on our end… Got to play better defense. Obviously, they’re hitting good shots and getting good looks. I think we were sped up a little bit, but we cleaned it up in the other quarters defensively. But can’t let that happen right out the gate. You need a sense of urgency. This is the WNBA Finals,” said Burton .

Valkyries must rediscover their defensive edge

The defeat was difficult for Burton personally, too. She finished with eight points on 2-of-13 shooting, alongside six rebounds and four assists.

A third-quarter flagrant foul, assessed after officials determined she made unnecessary contact with Rhyne Howard's face, added to her frustrating afternoon.

Head coach Natalie Nakase shared Burton's disappointment, describing the team's opening performance as unacceptable.

“I’m just trying to explain to you that we’re all right now not happy with how it started… And so I want to go back, give them their time right now to get their bodies right, get their mental right, get their nutrition right (and) let them just sit in it,” said Nakase .

Atlanta's leading players made the most of their opportunity. Allisha Gray scored a team-high 23 points, while Howard added 21. Angel Reese also delivered an impressive performance, recording 15 points and 14 rebounds to help the Dream keep their championship hopes alive.

Despite the disappointing result, Golden State found some positives. After trailing by as many as 25 points, the Valkyries fought back and outscored Atlanta in both second-half quarters.

They also won the rebounding battle 36-35 and committed fewer turnovers, demonstrating that they hadn't completely lost their competitive edge.

Now, everything comes down to Game 7 in San Francisco. The Valkyries must rediscover the defensive intensity that helped them take control of the series if they want to claim the title on home court.

articles.title: Angel Reese’s “Sit down, you’re on the bench” taunt puts WNBA Finals officiating in the spotlight
articles.standfirst: Reese delivers the taunt in front of a referee as the WNBA Finals head to a winner-take-all Game 7
articles.summary: Reese delivers the taunt in front of a referee as the WNBA Finals head to a winner-take-all Game 7
articles.body:
Angel Reese delivers a pointed message to the Golden State Valkyries just before a free throw: “Sit down, you’re on the bench.” The Atlanta Dream forward makes the remark while the referee stands nearby with the ball. He appears to watch the exchange, then hands it to Reese so she can take her shot.

The moment is drawing attention not just because of what Reese says, but because of when she says it. The official is right in front of her, yet the sequence continues without an apparent warning or interruption. That leaves fans asking where the line is between heated competition and behavior an official should address.

Reese’s fire is part of the story and part of the risk

Angel has never been shy about playing with emotion, and the clip captures that edge in full view. Her intensity can energize a team and add another layer to a high-stakes game. It can also invite scrutiny when the words are directed at an opponent in front of an official.

The contrast is especially noticeable after a difficult performance in the previous game, when Reese acknowledged her mistakes . In this clip, she is back to the forceful, confrontational style fans have come to associate with her. Whether it rattles an opponent or simply reflects her competitive personality.

The referee’s response is just as striking. Officials have to manage the game as well as call fouls , and visible confrontations can quickly affect its tone. The video does not show the referee stepping in before Reese takes the free throw, leaving viewers to debate whether the exchange crossed a line.

The game will be available to watch in the U.S. on ESPN and ABC, with streaming on the ESPN app. Game 7 tips off Saturday, Oct. 31, at 6 p.m. CT from Chase Center in San Francisco, where the Golden State Valkyries host the Atlanta Dream with the series tied 3-3.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham recalls getting a black eye from a $5,000 handbag while protecting Brittney Griner
articles.standfirst: Cunningham recalls a chaotic airport encounter that turned into a painful memory
articles.summary: Cunningham recalls a chaotic airport encounter that turned into a painful memory
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has revealed a painful but amusing story from her early WNBA career, recalling how an attempt to protect former Phoenix Mercury teammate Brittney Griner at an airport resulted in her getting a black eye from an expensive designer handbag.

The Indiana Fever guard shared the memorable experience during an appearance on Theo Von's This Past Weekend podcast.

While discussing the league's growing popularity and the challenges that come with increased attention, Cunningham reflected on her earlier days playing alongside some of basketball's biggest names.

During her time in Phoenix, Cunningham shared the court with Griner and Diana Taurasi . Both players attracted considerable public attention, but Griner's profile reached another level following her arrest in Russia in February 2022 over a cannabis oil vape cartridge discovered in her luggage.

Griner spent nearly 10 months in Russian custody before being released in December 2022 through a prisoner exchange involving Russian arms dealer Viktor Bout.

Her return to the United States generated enormous attention, making even routine public appearances difficult.

Cunningham recalled how teammates often found themselves responsible for protecting one another when crowds gathered around the Mercury's biggest stars. Security wasn't always readily available, leaving players to manage uncomfortable situations themselves.

Cunningham's attempt to protect Griner ended with an expensive accident

Describing the airport encounter, Cunningham explained that Griner was surrounded by people, prompting teammates to step in and create space around the center.

“There was this one guy who I guess was kind of our security, I don’t know. He was actually carrying her (Griner) Louis Vuitton bags,” said Cunningham .

“I was the caboose, and he saw what was happening. So he ran to push those people away, but when he did it, he threw the bags, and it came back and cracked me right in the nose.

“I was like I was trying to help, but I just get cracked by like a $5,000 bag right in my schnoz, black eye the next day.”

However, her podcast appearance also revealed a much darker side of becoming increasingly recognizable.

Cunningham disclosed that she believes approximately 20 individuals are being monitored by the FBI because of concerns involving her safety.

“The more you’re visible on TV, you’re going to get more fans,” Cunningham said. “People are going to know who you are, and that’s a really great thing. But there’s also a lot of like kind of crazy people, too. Like, we do have a lot of stalkers. I know I do.

“And that’s a negative side of things that people don’t think about. And so you do want to feel secure.”

One alleged stalker has faced felony charges involving stalking and intimidation in Indiana. Authorities have accused him of sending Cunningham unwanted messages and delivering a package addressed to her at the Fever's arena.

“The more you’re visible on TV, you’re going to get more fans,” Cunningham said. “People are going to know who you are, and that’s a really great thing. But there’s also a lot of like kind of crazy people, too. Like, we do have a lot of stalkers. I know I do.
“And that’s a negative side of things that people don’t think about. And so you do want to feel secure.”

One alleged stalker has faced felony charges involving stalking and intimidation in Indiana. Authorities have accused him of sending Cunningham unwanted messages and delivering a package addressed to her at the Fever's arena.

articles.title: Craze for the Nike Caitlin 1 ‘Jinx’ sneakers: Caitlin Clark's warning in limited-access sale
articles.standfirst: Clark launched her Halloween-themed shoe on October 30
articles.summary: Clark launched her Halloween-themed shoe on October 30
articles.body:
The release of Caitlin Clark ’s first signature sneaker took an unusual turn on Halloween weekend, as Nike restricted access to the Caitlin 1 Jinx edition and left most fans hoping for an invitation but the WNBA ace has a pointed warning for anyone trying to secure a pair.

The limited-edition colorway went on sale on October 30 through Nike ’s Exclusive Access system on the SNKRS app but rather than opening purchases to everyone, the company selected a limited number of members.

Creating frustration among collectors and basketball fans who had followed the release rumors for weeks with demand high, the Jinx quickly became one of the most talked-about sneaker drops of the Halloween season and is priced at $140.

Its restricted availability added to speculation about resale prices, with demand building around a shoe that combines the Indiana Fever star's personal story with seasonal details and performance features.

The name comes from a black cat that was part of Clark ’s childhood, and Nike incorporated that inspiration throughout the design as cat’s eyes appear on the tongue, while a witch graphic features on the insole.

Green accents and glow-in-the-dark elements give the shoe its Halloween identity and Clark also played along with the mystery in Nike ’s promotional campaign, suggesting that the shoes might glow when the lights go out.

“Good luck trying to get them,” Clark also quipped, indicating she is well aware of the demand for the sneaker whilst her comments added another layer to the launch, encouraging fans to discover the details for themselves.

Clark continues to deepen Nike collaboration

The Jinx arrives after Nike introduced the original Caitlin 1 , Clark ’s debut signature basketball shoe after the company unveiled that model on September 14, with its global release following on October 1 through Nike.com and selected retailers.

China received an earlier launch on September 24 and the shoe was developed around three priorities Clark identified for her game: a quicker first step, a faster step-back and a quicker release when shooting under pressure.

Its construction combines a lightweight Nike Opticast upper, Air Zoom Turbo cushioning in the forefoot and a Cushlon foam midsole whilst the Halloween edition builds on that foundation with a black mesh upper, metallic green detailing and shades of Ghost Green and Mint Foam .

Those elements, including the glow-in-the-dark accents, distinguish the Jinx from the original release as Clark ’s signature line continues to bloom and is the result of a partnership that began when she joined Nike as an athlete in 2022.

The relationship expanded in August 2025, when the company named her a signature athlete and introduced a personal logo built around two interlocking Cs whilst the collection also extended into apparel, with an 18-piece range featuring performance clothing and everyday sportswear.

Aero-FIT pieces were designed to improve cooling, while Standard Issue Stretch brought the brand’s basketball styling into women’s apparel.
